headlines.title: U.S. measles cases reach 35-year high in 2026, surpassing last year’s total
headlines.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported Friday that the United States has logged 2,318 measles cases in the first seven months of this year, surpassing last year’s total of 2,289.

headlines.title: How the cyclospora outbreak is impacting the food industry
headlines.description: A rise in cases of cyclosporiasis is causing people to steer clear of lettuce, while forcing salad restaurants and major fast-food chains to set the record straight.

headlines.title: Lebron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers
headlines.description: LeBron James has signed a 2-year $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers after becoming a free agent following his departure from the Los Angeles Lakers. NBC News' Rohan Nadkarni reports on James' "last decision."

headlines.title: White House Correspondents’ Dinner Returns Under High Security
headlines.description: President Donald Trump is gearing up to attend the rescheduled White House Correspondents Dinner Friday night, after the initial event back in April was targeted by a gunman. The Secret Service says it’s confident in the security plan for the dinner while also acknowledging an alarming rise in threats. NBC’s Garrett Haake reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Small businesses sue Trump administration to stop latest wave of tariffs
headlines.description: A group of small businesses on Friday sued the Trump administration over its latest tariffs on 60 U.S. trade partners, less than a day after they were enacted.

headlines.title: Franchise fatigue gives original stories a boost at Comic-Con
headlines.description: Comic-Con kicked off in San Diego on Thursday, and in a sign Hollywood may be moving beyond Peak IP, some of this year’s buzziest panels aren’t for superheroes or cute droids, but for visionary creators.

headlines.title: One month since dual earthquakes rocked Venezuela
headlines.description: One month after those horrific earthquakes rocked Venezuela, there are still questions surfacing about the government's emergency response. 5,398 are confirmed dead so far, with more than 29,000 still reported missing. NBC News' Gadi Schwartz speaks with survivors.

headlines.title: No basic services and nowhere to go: How Venezuelans are living a month after the earthquakes
headlines.description: We visited the ruins of a housing complex built by the Chavista regime: the now homeless residents brave the heat, humidity, and flies from their tents, as they’re promised a house by 2027.
